paras.text: Antiseptics and disinfectants are very similar in that they are both used for killing microorganisms although they differ in structure and uses.
paras.urdu: جراثیم کش (اینٹی سیپٹکس) اور ڈس انفیکٹنٹس اس لحاظ سے بہت ملتے جلتے ہیں کہ دونوں خرد جانداروں کو مارنے کے لیے استعمال ہوتے ہیں، اگرچہ ساخت اور استعمال میں مختلف ہیں۔
paras.pashto: انټي سېپټیکونه او ډس انفېکټنټونه په دې کې ډېر ورته دي چې دواړه د مایکرو ارګانیزمونو د وژلو لپاره کارېږي، که څه هم په جوړښت او کارونه کې توپیر لري.

paras.text: Antiseptics are used on living organisms, such as human skin, to kill any microorganisms living on the bodies’ surface. Disinfectants are used on non-living things, such as countertops and handrails, to kill the microorganisms living on that inanimate surface. Antiseptics are typically found to have a lower concentration of the particular biocide which is used in that product to clean the surface other than that of a disinfectant. Since the disinfectants are not meant for use on living tissues, but rather inanimate surfaces, they can use the higher concentration of biocide in the product since there is no skin or tissue to worry about irritation. Antiseptics require the lower concentration of biocide as too high concentrations of certain biocides could cause high amounts of skin irritation.
paras.urdu: اینٹی سیپٹکس جانداروں، جیسے انسانی جلد، پر جسم کی سطح پر رہنے والے خرد جانداروں کو مارنے کے لیے استعمال ہوتے ہیں۔ ڈس انفیکٹنٹس بے جان چیزوں، جیسے کاؤنٹر ٹاپس اور ریلنگ، پر اس بے جان سطح پر رہنے والے خرد جانداروں کو مارنے کے لیے استعمال ہوتے ہیں۔ اینٹی سیپٹکس میں عموماً اس مخصوص حیات کش مادے کا ارتکاز ڈس انفیکٹنٹ سے کم ہوتا ہے۔ چونکہ ڈس انفیکٹنٹس زندہ بافتوں کے بجائے بے جان سطحوں کے لیے ہیں، اس لیے ان میں حیات کش کا زیادہ ارتکاز استعمال ہو سکتا ہے کیونکہ جلد یا بافت میں جلن کی فکر نہیں ہوتی۔ اینٹی سیپٹکس کو حیات کش کا کم ارتکاز درکار ہے کیونکہ بعض حیات کشوں کا بہت زیادہ ارتکاز جلد میں شدید جلن پیدا کر سکتا ہے۔

paras.text: It is essential for people to know the difference between antiseptics and disinfectants since they are both used for similar things but in different ways. Using a disinfectant as an antiseptic would likely irritate that tissue. Also, using an antiseptic as a disinfectant could result in a less sufficient job of cleaning that surface due to the lower concentration of biocide. Extreme caution must be taken to avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes. The negative effect of disinfectant is that it is caustic to the skin, lungs and eyes.

sections.theory:
Society, Technology And Science

Antiseptics and disinfectants are very similar in that they are both used for killing microorganisms although they differ in structure and uses.

Antiseptics are used on living organisms, such as human skin, to kill any microorganisms living on the bodies’ surface. Disinfectants are used on non-living things, such as countertops and handrails, to kill the microorganisms living on that inanimate surface. Antiseptics are typically found to have a lower concentration of the particular biocide which is used in that product to clean the surface other than that of a disinfectant. Since the disinfectants are not meant for use on living tissues, but rather inanimate surfaces, they can use the higher concentration of biocide in the product since there is no skin or tissue to worry about irritation. Antiseptics require the lower concentration of biocide as too high concentrations of certain biocides could cause high amounts of skin irritation.

Some examples of antiseptics are mouthwash or hand sanitizer, both of which are safe to come in contact with your skin and also are able to be extremely effective at killing high amounts of microorganisms.

Phenols, bleach and formaldehyde are all examples of different types of disinfectants used to kill the microorganisms on the surface of any non-living objects.

It is essential for people to know the difference between antiseptics and disinfectants since they are both used for similar things but in different ways. Using a disinfectant as an antiseptic would likely irritate that tissue. Also, using an antiseptic as a disinfectant could result in a less sufficient job of cleaning that surface due to the lower concentration of biocide. Extreme caution must be taken to avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes. The negative effect of disinfectant is that it is caustic to the skin, lungs and eyes.

Key Points

Alcohols are compounds, in which a hydroxyl group (–OH) is attached to aliphatic carbon atom.

Hydroxyl group is attached to aromatic carbon atoms in phenols.

Lucas test is used to distinguish between primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols.

The formation of ester from alcohol and carboxylic acid is called “esterification”.

Each carbon atom in phenol is sp²-hybridized.

Dow process is used for preparation of phenol from chlorobenzene and aqueous NaOH at high pressure and temperature.

Ethers are a class of compounds in which, with oxygen atom two alkyl groups, two aryl groups or one alkyl and one aryl group are attached.

General formula of ether is R–O–R.

Ethers react with cold conc. HCl or H₂SO₄ to form oxonium salt.

In Williamson synthesis method, sodium alkoxide is treated with an alkyl halide to produce ether.

Hydrogen bonding in alcohols result in relatively high boiling points and good miscibility with water.

اینٹی سیپٹکس جانداروں، جیسے انسانی جلد، پر جسم کی سطح پر رہنے والے خرد جانداروں کو مارنے کے لیے استعمال ہوتے ہیں۔ ڈس انفیکٹنٹس بے جان چیزوں، جیسے کاؤنٹر ٹاپس اور ریلنگ، پر اس بے جان سطح پر رہنے والے خرد جانداروں کو مارنے کے لیے استعمال ہوتے ہیں۔ اینٹی سیپٹکس میں عموماً اس مخصوص حیات کش مادے کا ارتکاز ڈس انفیکٹنٹ سے کم ہوتا ہے۔ چونکہ ڈس انفیکٹنٹس زندہ بافتوں کے بجائے بے جان سطحوں کے لیے ہیں، اس لیے ان میں حیات کش کا زیادہ ارتکاز استعمال ہو سکتا ہے کیونکہ جلد یا بافت میں جلن کی فکر نہیں ہوتی۔ اینٹی سیپٹکس کو حیات کش کا کم ارتکاز درکار ہے کیونکہ بعض حیات کشوں کا بہت زیادہ ارتکاز جلد میں شدید جلن پیدا کر سکتا ہے۔

sections.content:
Society, Technology And Science

Antiseptics and disinfectants are very similar in that they are both used for killing microorganisms although they differ in structure and uses.

Antiseptics are used on living organisms, such as human skin, to kill any microorganisms living on the bodies’ surface. Disinfectants are used on non-living things, such as countertops and handrails, to kill the microorganisms living on that inanimate surface. Antiseptics are typically found to have a lower concentration of the particular biocide which is used in that product to clean the surface other than that of a disinfectant. Since the disinfectants are not meant for use on living tissues, but rather inanimate surfaces, they can use the higher concentration of biocide in the product since there is no skin or tissue to worry about irritation. Antiseptics require the lower concentration of biocide as too high concentrations of certain biocides could cause high amounts of skin irritation.

Some examples of antiseptics are mouthwash or hand sanitizer, both of which are safe to come in contact with your skin and also are able to be extremely effective at killing high amounts of microorganisms.

Phenols, bleach and formaldehyde are all examples of different types of disinfectants used to kill the microorganisms on the surface of any non-living objects.

It is essential for people to know the difference between antiseptics and disinfectants since they are both used for similar things but in different ways. Using a disinfectant as an antiseptic would likely irritate that tissue. Also, using an antiseptic as a disinfectant could result in a less sufficient job of cleaning that surface due to the lower concentration of biocide. Extreme caution must be taken to avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes. The negative effect of disinfectant is that it is caustic to the skin, lungs and eyes.

Key Points

Alcohols are compounds, in which a hydroxyl group (–OH) is attached to aliphatic carbon atom.

Hydroxyl group is attached to aromatic carbon atoms in phenols.

Lucas test is used to distinguish between primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols.

The formation of ester from alcohol and carboxylic acid is called “esterification”.

Each carbon atom in phenol is sp²-hybridized.

Dow process is used for preparation of phenol from chlorobenzene and aqueous NaOH at high pressure and temperature.

Ethers are a class of compounds in which, with oxygen atom two alkyl groups, two aryl groups or one alkyl and one aryl group are attached.

General formula of ether is R–O–R.

Ethers react with cold conc. HCl or H₂SO₄ to form oxonium salt.

In Williamson synthesis method, sodium alkoxide is treated with an alkyl halide to produce ether.

Hydrogen bonding in alcohols result in relatively high boiling points and good miscibility with water.
